beats.say: Everyone slips: taps a link, reads out a code. What matters is the next five minutes.
Do not hide it and do not try to fix it alone. A silent mistake gives the attacker time.
Be honest: what you tapped, what you typed, what you said. The specialist needs to know.
Then specialists lock the account and check the device. The aim is to stop the harm, not to find someone to blame.

nodes.text: The caller said he was technical support and you read out the code sent to your phone. After the call you had doubts.

choices.label: I call the support number I know at once
choices.feedback: Correct. Every minute counts, the attacker may already be signing in.

choices.label: I am embarrassed and tell nobody
choices.feedback: The attacker is now in your account and nobody knows. Silence makes it worse.

choices.label: I change the password myself, that is enough
choices.feedback: A good step, but not enough. The attacker may stay in an open session that a specialist must end.

nodes.text: When did you give the code and what else did the caller want?
nodes.speaker: Security team
nodes.spoken: When did you give the code <breath> and what else did the caller want?

choices.label: I tell everything as it was, including the code
choices.feedback: Correct. With honest details the specialist knows exactly what to lock.

choices.label: I say there was just a call, I gave no code
choices.feedback: With half the story the specialist does not know the account was taken. Honesty saves time.

nodes.text: The specialist ended all sessions and asked you to set a new password. Your manager asks: what happened?

choices.label: I explain openly so the team is warned too
choices.feedback: Excellent. Your story protects colleagues from the same call.

choices.label: I say nothing happened
choices.feedback: The same call may reach your colleagues. Speaking up protects them.

scenes.title: The next day
scenes.intro: Yesterday you opened a fake link and reported it. Today three emails are waiting in your inbox.

body.text: Thank you for reporting. All open sessions on your account have been ended.
Today, change your password on the organisation's portal. We send no link: open the portal yourself.

actions.label: Mark as safe
actions.feedback: Correct. The address is your organisation's, there is no link and nothing is asked.

actions.label: Report as phishing
actions.feedback: Caution is good, but this one is genuine: your organisation's address and no link.

body.text: After yesterday's incident, confirm your account again within one hour.

steps.say: Attackers sometimes write a second time.

actions.label: Report as phishing
actions.feedback: Correct, the address is not your organisation's domain. Attackers often come back to the same person.

actions.label: Open the link
actions.feedback: That was a second trap. The real team asked you to change the password on the portal yourself.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: You are safe, but this email shows the attack is still going on. Report it.

subject.text: A strange email came from you

body.text: Hello, last night an email called "Invoice" came from your address with a link in it. Did you send it?

actions.label: Forward to the security team
actions.feedback: Correct. If the attacker wrote to others from your account, specialists must know.

actions.label: Reply: not me, do not open it
actions.feedback: Good, you warned your colleague. Forward it to the security team as well.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Your colleague may open the link and the specialist will not know the attack spread.

scenes.prompt: What usually happens after you report? Put it in order.

items.label: The specialist locks the account and ends sessions
The computer and mailbox are checked
You set a new password and get back to work

scenes.explain: This is the normal routine. The sooner you report, the shorter it is.

question.prompt: A colleague says: "If I report it, I will be told off." What do you answer?

options.label: Reporting fast limits the harm, hiding it makes it bigger
options.feedback: Correct. Fast, honest information is the most valuable help for specialists.

options.label: You are right, let nobody know
options.feedback: A hidden mistake grows and can harm the whole organisation.

options.label: Try to fix it yourself first
options.feedback: Fixing it alone can destroy traces and lose time.

scenes.explain: Silence, not the mistake, makes the danger grow.

points: If you slipped, report it at once and honestly.
Watch the next emails: the attacker may write again.
The aim is to stop the harm, not to find someone to blame.
